At least the cumulus dragon is up there wearing a satisfied smirk due to its penchant for tricking cloud-gazers. Then again, maybe it's daydreaming of Kraken Kabbage… *wistful sigh*
dragons.Goal: A cloud dragon, indeed, but not one to rain on your parade!

dragons.Name: Tulip
dragons.Description: Ah, the tulip dragon. The witch nicknamed Miniscule Minervina was the first to stumble over this dragon—quite literally, as the dragon was napping in a tulip field. Blended right in! That's where magicfolk get the old cautionary phrase "It's better to tiptoe through the tulips." Especially handy advice in the garden in the moonlight.
dragons.Goal: This dragon seems to be having a wonderful time!

dragons.Name: Pond
dragons.Description: More than one wizard has sat by a pond dragon and thought it just an ordinary pond—imagine the surprise when that pond flew away! Even in a land as magical as the Vale, that's just something you don't see every day.
dragons.Goal: Do you think the pond dragon and the salamander dragon hang out?

dragons.Name: Sumi
dragons.Description: A most peculiar thing happened when the witch Sora Terasu was tasked with studying the sakura dragon. The day seemed ordinary enough—the scent of blossoms on the breeze, a herd of plains dragons making its way across a distant field, the sounds of magical explosions from the Great Nogard's workshop—as she set off on the path to Cherry Heights. What Sora saw along her route stopped her in her tracks: writing in the sky, as if inked of clouds! She stood gaping at the sight of these unfamiliar runes, wondering what magical artist was behind the apparition. Suddenly, a brush-tailed dragon rocketed through the air, leaving a spellbinding trail of ink blots in its wake. “Sumi,” Sora mused to herself as she watched, recalling a variety of ink used in the timeless art of wand wash painting. “I shall call you sumi!”
dragons.Goal: Now that's a tail with a tale!

dragons.Name: Plateau
dragons.Description: One of the most docile dragons in the Vale is the plateau dragon. These slow-moving behemoths will often plop down for hours on end, flexing nary a scale as they soak up the sunshine. In fact, they're so un-botherable, they've been known to let little Valekins climb around on their heads. The kids call it “Summiting”—first one to the top wins! But don't worry—the magical markers of the hidden habitat will keep the kids at bay in your park.
dragons.Goal: We could all stand to be a little more like the plateau dragon, don't you think?

dragons.Name: Frostflower
dragons.Description: As dragons go, the frostflower is a very particular creature. It tends to reveal itself in the wild only when conditions are *just* right—cold, but not too cold, and dark, but not too dark, and covered, but not too covered. And they're shy, to boot—sheesh! If you were to sneak up on an unsuspecting herd of frostflowers, you can be certain they'd flee faster than an iceberg dragon in a fire habitat. But don't do that! That's just cold.
dragons.Goal: You're part-way to a bouquet!

dragons.Name: Nova
dragons.Description: Brilliant though the astromancer Noel dePlante may be, it took the help of light magic experts Shi Nee and Ylyse Draagg to discover the nova dragon. In the roiling cauldron that is the cosmos, only a specific set of complex spells can reveal this elusive galaxy dragon. This magical detection technique is known as Draagg's Divination!
dragons.Goal: Did you see this one coming?

dragons.Name: Singularity
dragons.Description: When you look at the singularity dragon, you're not seeing the dragon, but an outline caused by magical waves distorting *around* the dragon. It's true! The singularity dragon itself has no visible form. You can thank astromancer Sven Sparrowing for that mind-bending bit of magical theory. He witnessed the distortions while stargazing one particularly clear night, and has been confusing people with his discovery ever since.
dragons.Goal: ...one giant leap for dragonkind!

dragons.Name: Cyclone
dragons.Description: Valefolk thought they were in for a second Cataclysm when a series of terrible tornadoes tore through the skies of the Witchitoto Plains. Worried the destruction would reach inhabited villages, a band of brave witches and wizards gathered to investigate. Lead by volunteer Dorothea Wynd, the group made for the plains and set to studying the unusual cyclonic phenomenon. As they observed, they discovered this was no ordinary cyclone, but a cyclone dragon! The poor creature was dazzled by a hypnotic dragon, and had been stuck tornadoing through Witchitoto ever since. Thankfully, a simple right-round spell gave the cyclone dragon control of its movement again. What a whirlwind adventure!
dragons.Goal: There's no place like home—especially in such a nice habitat!

dragons.Name: Shining
dragons.Description: While traveling through the mountainous region of Setse, the wizard Torrance Jaxxon stumbled upon a set of twin omen dragons cavorting through the woods. “Come and play with us!” they seemed to say with their adorable antics. Intrigued, Torrance followed them through the labyrinthian corridors of trees until he found himself in a clearing. There, illuminated by the glow of the moon, stood the most unusual dragon Torrance had ever seen! Like an ethereal conjuring from the pages of a storyscroll, the dragon stood in an almost kingly posture, emitting a brilliant shine. Alas, when Torrance reached into his pockets for a Dragon Treat, he found only a flask of orange juice. The shining dragon must have had other interests, for it quickly fled into the frozen night.
dragons.Goal: It's important to spend time with your dragons! “All work and no play makes Stanley a dull wizard,” as the saying goes.

dragons.Name: Jetstream
dragons.Description: Some Valefolk—the type typically prone to wearing pointy aluminum hats—believe the jetstream dragon plays some sort of role in the infamous Cataclysm Causality conspiracy theory. Of course, that theory is just silly—the jetstream dragon has no agenda but to snack on Dragon Treats and show off for visitors. ...at least, we're pretty sure that's the case, but it's hard to tell from inside of this magical bunker.
dragons.Goal: Don't fly off the handle over the rumors surrounding this dragon.

dragons.Name: Fissure
dragons.Description: Nestled deep within Laki Chasm is a cave. Within that cave is a lake. And at the bottom of that lake is yet another cave. And within that cave at the bottom of the lake in the cave is yet *another* lake. And—well, you get the idea. It goes on for quite a while. Such is the perilous path to reach the home of the fissure dragon, deep in the earthen core of the chasm. The only wizard up for the journey wasn't a wizard at all, but a witch named Penny Syll (“Pen” for short). As it turns out, she was just trying to find a quiet place to do some spellwriting—wasn't even trying to discover a dragon. What luck!
dragons.Goal: The most fascinating discoveries seem to happen by accident, don't they?

dragons.Name: Surge
dragons.Description: What causes the unusual glow pattern of the surge dragon? Magic, of course! Haven't you been paying attention to the way things work around here?
dragons.Goal: We'll leave it up to you to make the obligatory “It's like magic!” joke.

dragons.Name: Steam
dragons.Description:
From the Scrolls of Pi Roh's Ponderings:

There once was a dragon called steam
Whose breath blast was something supreme
With water and fire
An ephemeral spire
Like something straight out of a dream!
dragons.Goal: What a hot addition to your collection!

dragons.Name: Plant Rift
dragons.Description: Rift-brushed dragons like the plant rift are unique in that their development occurred from contact with low-grade chaotic magic. It's an enchanting idea, isn't it? Though the effort to contain the Rift caused a great deal of panic in the Vale, great innovations came out of the chaos. One could apply the same theory to life!
dragons.Goal: Gardenia can't wait to study this one!

dragons.Name: Fire Rift
dragons.Description: What a dragon! Gwyddion the Great Nogard theorizes that the fire rift dragon was once an ordinary fire dragon who encountered chaos magic from the Rift. Fortunately, the potency of this chaos magic seems to be on the low end; the only effects observed so far have been decorative. Maybe keep an eye on this li'l fella, though, lest it develop... other... Rift qualities.
dragons.Goal: This Rift-brushed dragon is out of this world!

dragons.Name: Blightwing
dragons.Description: Little is known about the fascinating dragons that developed in the Rift, and the blightwing dragon is no exception. If only we could ask the dragon to tell us about its time in the Rift! ...actually, is there even time in the Rift? That's a timeless debate among Rift scholars. What might the blightwing dragon say if it could weigh in on the subject? Another unknowable to ponder!
dragons.Goal: Do you think there are pumpermelons in the Rift?

dragons.Name: Voltaic
dragons.Description: The voltaic dragon certainly made quite an entrance into the Vale when it emerged from the Rift. A thunderous cacophony accompanied its arrival, and with it some of the fiercest rains in Vale memory. But for all the voltaic's pomp and circumstance, this is one scaredy dragon—the terrifying sound of its own thunderous arrival sent it scurrying into a nearby cave. Gwyddion the Great Nogard depleted an entire plot of pumpermelons trying to coax it back out!
dragons.Goal: As intense-looking as it is shy, which is quite the combination!

dragons.Name: Snowsquall
dragons.Description: Dragons in the Rift have developed strange and unusual features to deal with the Rift's wonky wibbles and wobbles. Coping with this chaos magic seems to have lead to the sprouting of tentacles on the snowsquall dragon's face. Some folk might be inclined to say “Ew,” but that's awfully rude. You might sprout tentacles, too, if you spent long enough in the Rift!
dragons.Goal: Spententacular!

dragons.Name: Spore
dragons.Description: When the spore dragon emerged from the Rift, Gwyddion the Great Nogard couldn't believe his eyes. “We haven't seen a dragon from the Rift since Light and Dark magic returned to the Vale!” he exclaimed to Gardenia, who was first in line to study this dragon's unusual patterning of mushroomscales. What wonders!
dragons.Goal: Wonder what else lurks in the Rift...

dragons.Name: Alpenglow
dragons.Description: The alpenglow dragon is so named for a phenomenon in the Rift that occurs when light reflects off of pockets of chaos magic to beautiful effect. A similar light effect seems to occur in this dragon's horns and belly, as though lit with an internal alpenglow. Gwyddion the Great Nogard believes this inner lamplight allows the alpenglow dragon to navigate even the darkest corners of the Rift.
dragons.Goal: You're glowing over this dragon!

dragons.Name: Infrared
dragons.Description: There's more to this dragon than meets the eye. Look closely at the adult infrared's belly, and you might notice a familiar hatchling form. No, no, don't worry—the infrared dragon doesn't consume hatchlings. What a silly notion! Rather, as this dragon ages, it blossoms plumes of magical smokescales to build its grown-up dragony shape. Such is the awesome power of concentrated fire magic!
dragons.Goal: We're positively glowing over this dragon!

dragons.Name: Earth Rift
dragons.Description: One thing is true of earth dragons and earth rift dragons alike: they're a grounded bunch. The earth dragon's brush with chaotic Rift magic might have changed its appearance, but the old adage still applies. Gwyddion the Great Nogard is heartened by this idea. “Perhaps this means that chaos magic on the Surface below has dissipated to harmless levels, too,” he mused to Gardenia. “Someone should go down there and find out!”
dragons.Goal: You know what they say: you can cast a flying spell on an earth rift dragon, but you can't make it flap.

dragons.Name: Cold Rift
dragons.Description: Sporting a dapper coat of furscales, the cold rift dragon has no problems keeping warm in the freezey-cold pockets of the Rift. Also handy are the eyes of this dragon, which dim the otherwise impassable glare of the Rift's icy chaos caves, and allow the cold rift dragon to take residence inside. Gwyddion the Great Nogard is amazed by this adaptability. “We could learn a thing or two from the development of these clever dragons!”
dragons.Goal: Would you say this is a cool dragon? It's okay, the Parliament for the Prevention of Painful Puns isn't listening.

dragons.Name: Snapper
dragons.Description: Some believe the snapper dragon is at the center of an unusual legend about the origin of the world. So it's told, the Surface land from whence the Vale islands were carved rests on the back of a giant shelled dragon. And that dragon, too, rests on the back of another shelled dragon. And what do you know—that dragon, in turn, rests on the back of yet *another* shelled dragon. And what, you ask, does that dragon teeter atop? Why, it's shelled dragons all the way down! So the legend goes, anyway.
dragons.Goal: There's a snappy something to be said about this dragon, surely.

dragons.Name: Lightning Rift
dragons.Description: Lightning magic doesn't behave in the Rift as we're used to seeing in the Vale. Rather than conducting through metal, the lightning appears to merely bounce off of everything it encounters. Good news for the lightning rift dragon—no need to worry about crashing into things mid-flight when you bounce right back.
dragons.Goal: No Rift can keep this dragon down–it'll bounce right back!

dragons.Name: Water Rift
dragons.Description: Does the Rift have oceans? Lakes? Ponds? Streams? Little is known about the geography within the Rift, but if the water rift dragon is any indication, there's bound to be water in there somewhere. Heck, maybe there's a portal in the depths of the Rift's oceans that leads to the Surface waters below the Vale! Maybe keep an eye on this dragon—track its whereabouts, see what it knows. You never know, you know?
dragons.Goal: No rift, not even one with a capital R, can stand between a collector and their dragons.

dragons.Name: Air Rift
dragons.Description: There's something in the air… oh, it's an air rift dragon! That would make sense, wouldn't it? Unless the inside of the Rift is some sort of bizzaro world in which water dragons fly and air dragons float. But that's preposterous… isn't it? Is it? Question everything! Just don't expect the air rift dragon to answer.
dragons.Goal: This dragon is a breath of fresh air! Smells rifty.

dragons.Name: Metal Rift
dragons.Description: Do you hear a killer rock'n'roll guitar riff when you look at this dragon? No? Just Gwyddion? He might be hexed—someone should help him. Anyway, the metal rift dragon is a tenacious sort. Most dragons play well with others, but the metal rift dragon seems to prefer going solo. As the songwriter witch Jill White sings, “The metal has its way.”
dragons.Goal: Are you sure you don't hear a guitar riff when you look at this dragon? Hmmm, must be a hex.

dragons.Name: Arid
dragons.Description: When you're an itty bitty thing like the arid dragon, it helps to have some extra armor on your side. It seems these dragons employ a magical exoskeleton to avoid being tromped on by their bigger brethren. If ever you're wandering Sandara Desert and see these empty exoskeletons lying about, fear not! Like little Valers outgrowing their school robes, sometimes the arid dragon needs to upgrade its duds.
dragons.Goal: Make no bones about it, this dragon will get even the most introverted of wizards out of their shells!

dragons.Name: Zaffer
dragons.Description: What gives Rift-touched dragons like the zaffer such unusual pulsating patterns? Excellent question! Gwyddion is doing his best to figure it out, with the help of the Vale's brightest magical minds. The short answer is "chaos magic," but Gwyddion isn't quite sure why or how. Perhaps the Etherium powering the Rift Breeding Cave has something to do with it. Additional alchemical analysis is advised.
dragons.Goal: Nothing like a new dragon to chase away the blues!

dragons.Name: Viridian
dragons.Description: We wizards are just as surprised as you might be by the viridian dragon. Little is known about what happens in the Rift, though the Valefolk are working night and day to understand exactly how its chaotic magics work. So far, the viridian dragon seems to be pretty normal—it's not terrorizing villages or nomming townspeople, which is always nice when it comes to dragons from other dimensions. Interestingly, the viridian's back appears to be covered in armor-like scales. Perhaps the viridian evolved to withstand debris storms within the Rift—or maybe it just likes to look cool for its Rift friends. There's so much to learn about these dragons!
dragons.Goal: What a Rifty dragon!

dragons.Name: Plumewing
dragons.Description: The witch Ally Tanco was the first to breed the plumewing after the stabilization of the Rift. You should know this about Ally: she dresses EXCLUSIVELY in gold and silver, and the day of the plumewing's discovery was no exception. When the plumewing hatched and saw the mesmerizing metallic materials of Ally's fashion choices, it flew about in a dizzying tizzy, squawking so excitedly, Ally feared the hatchling would faint. Whatever the reason, it seems plumewing dragons REALLY like shiny things. Like, really really. You might want to warn visitors to keep an eye on any loose change in their pockets.
dragons.Goal: They say dragons who like shiny things bring good luck. Treasure it!

dragons.Name: Kampos
dragons.Description: The kampos dragon invokes a children's tale oft told in the Vale. According to this legend, a mysterious dragon with tentacled wings and an armored tail would find young witches and wizards lost in the wilds, then ferry them to safety upon its back. Given the uncanny resemblance to the dragon of legend, Gwyddion decided to call this Rift-brushed dragon “kampos,” from the phrase "hippicus kampicus," a term in the old tongue meaning "one who rescues." Looks like you turned the tables on the legend by rescuing kampos from the wilds of the Rift!
dragons.Goal: Another day, another dragon!

dragons.Name: Antumbra
dragons.Description:
Gwyddion's Field Notes on Dragons of the Rift:

“Witnessed the hatching of an antumbra dragon. Appears to sport exoscales for protection from Rift debris. Squeezey-pincery face is of the adorable variety. Luminous hindquarters may serve as a nightlight in scary Rift regions. Pronounced pumpermelon penchant proven—pockets pilfered.”
dragons.Goal: What an exo-traordinary dragon!

dragons.Name: Ghast
dragons.Description:
The great Vale poet Hy Koo was so taken with the ghast dragon, he couldn't help but pen a stanza:

Skull-horn'ed dragon
A phantasm of the Rift
Drifts upon the gales
dragons.Goal: We're aghast we didn't discover this dragon sooner!

dragons.Name: Solarflare
dragons.Description:
This dragon is gifted to all players who reach park level 100.

A solarflare dragon?! Astonishing! These dragons only appear when a park proprietor reaches a magnificent milestone! Legend has it, one must showcase a near immeasurable amount of park prowess to obtain a solarflare dragon. According to the ancient and mysterious Book of Documents, were such an amount of prowess to be measureable, that number would be 100. “Ninety-nine,” the Book of Documents reads, “one shall not measure, excepting that one then proceeds to 100. 101 is right out.” Clearly, that's no ordinary dragon.
dragons.Goal: Extraordinary! What a dragon!

dragons.Name: Ironwrought
dragons.Description: What a pinnacle of strength! The wizard Fe Brinell first discovered the ironwrought dragon when he witnessed it pull a prodigious patch of pumpermelons out of the ground in one sweeping mouthful! And talk about a timely discovery — what better dragon to be found on the 6th anniversary of the opening of the Vale's parks than one of such might? A park proprietor like yourself knows just how much care and effort goes into maintaining your fleet of floating islands and the dragons who call them home. The ironwrought dragon is a strong symbol of that mettle, wouldn't you say? Really carries a weight!
dragons.Goal: *trumpet fanfare* Happy birthday, DragonVale!

dragons.Name: Thunderbird
dragons.Description: The thunderbird dragon's favorite type of food is one no treat farm produces: lightning! This dragon has been spotted gobbling up stray bolts and blasts, giving rise to questions as numerous as they are reasonable: Wait, what? Is that a Rift thing? Doesn't that hurt? How is that nutritious? Or even delicious? In fact, what does lightning taste like? How much lightning can a dragon eat? What if it ate ALL of the lightning ever? How rumbly would its tummy be? Thunderous implications! Well, at least we can answer the question of where this dragon gets its name.
dragons.Goal: How does this dragon strike you?

dragons.Name: Lacuna
dragons.Description: In the old tongue, “lacuna” means “lake of the abyss” — and it was in the abyss of the Rift that the wizard Anne T. Matre discovered the lacuna dragon. The clever witch, an expert in revealing hidden things, devised a spell to track dragons in the miasmic ether. After some time spent following what turned out to be Gwyddion in a dragon disguise (he, too, has his ways of finding dragons), Anne happened upon the luminous glow of the lacuna. She was so transfixed by the dragon's flowing tail, so much like the coral that once grew in the Surface oceans, she nearly lost her way back! Well, at least she could've kept Roger company.
dragons.Goal: That is one impressive tail!

dragons.Name: Dandelion
dragons.Description:
From the scrolls of the poet Hy Koo:

Fluffy wisps and wings
Breeze-floating dandelion
Dreaming of blushrooms
dragons.Goal: Do you think these dragons have something to do with the springtime weather?

dragons.Name: Icebound
dragons.Description: "Ah, ze hidden depths of ze icebound dragon," writes wizard documentarian Henre Zerwog in his famous scroll, Encounters on ze Ice. "Zere are many cold dragons, but none such as zis—a true behemoth of ze ice, like somezing from a long-ago era. Zee how ze coat of icescales on its back protects ze delicate liquidscales beneath—magnificent magic. We are truly fortunate to witness a dragon of such substance."
dragons.Goal: Does the awesomeness of this dragon give you ze chills, too?

dragons.Name: Spirit
dragons.Description: Folkloric tales of this dragon echo through time and tradition. As it's told, the first spirit dragon appeared before a witch who was lost in the fogs of the Drag Marshes. The spirit dragon tried to use its breath to show the wayward witch which way to go, but its exhalations can only be seen by those in tune with the dragon's ethereal nature. With some clever conjuring, the lost witch was able to give the dragon a special runewand through which it could blast its beautiful blue breath for all to behold. To this day, some say spirit dragons still inhabit places where folk are likely to get lost, using their benevolent breaths to guide home wayward wanderers.
dragons.Goal: Why, this dragon must have been in plain sight all along! Amazing!

dragons.Name: Oni
dragons.Description: Oni dragons may look like they can live in any stark environment, but in actuality they love a comfortable den made of found objects around the Vale. Leaves, scraps of yarn, and even discarded Valefolk clothing are ideal for their makeshift bedding. Gwyddion the Great Nogard claims to have seen one lash out during this odd ritual. The oni dragon was diligently crafting its sleeping quarters when tree branches whirled in from a westward wind and decimated the dragon's hard work. The oni dragon drew its club-like tail back and, with one fell swoop, shattered them into a thousand pieces. It is rumored that the oni dragon smirked and started over again.
dragons.Goal: A comfy home is all the oni dragon needs in order to be happy! Nice job!

dragons.Name: Dracabra
dragons.Description: Tales from legend inspired a coven of witches to follow a seemingly lost baby dracabra dragon. They followed its erratic flight until it took rest high atop a tree. There, it clung to a branch and hung upside-down, wary of its observers. The coven dispersed for fear of spooking the young creature. The witches returned when dawn broke and were astonished to find a fully grown dragon! Somehow, the dracabra had managed to sneak off and gorge itself on treats, growing to full size overnight!
dragons.Goal: I had heard of these dragons, but never did I think I'd actually see one! Your visitors will love it!

dragons.Name: Gargoyle
dragons.Description: Gardenia was befuddled when treats started to go missing from her garden. After closer inspection, she discovered a Gargoyle dragon impersonating a statue among her zazzberry bushes! These sneaky dragons can stand still for long stretches of time, bolting to snatch a mouthful of treats while your back is turned and returning to their original position as soon as you turn to look.  Don't blink; they move so fast you might miss it!
dragons.Goal: Do you suppose if we blink we'll mistake the gargoyle dragon for a statue?

dragons.Name: Frostfluff
dragons.Description:
Gwyddion's Field Notes from the Rift:

“Day 5 in the Rift. Adopted a dragon disguise to track a new Rift-touched dragon. Am observing from a distance so as not to disturb its natural behavior. Seems to be primarily of the Cold trait family. Appears to be incredibly fluffy and adorable. Must quell urge to abandon disguise and pinch cheeks. Temptation proving increasingly difficult to keep at bay. So… cute… cannot… resist… tiny… baby… fluffface…”
dragons.Goal: That is one adorable dragon you've hatched there!

dragons.Name: Nesting
dragons.Description: Now here's an unusual dragon! Or shall we say set of dragons? Currently being studied by Matryona Starling, the nesting dragon seems to be equipped with a pouch in which it carries its little dragonling friends. Which begs the questions: do those dragonlings, too, have their own pouches containing yet smaller dragons within? And do those yet smaller dragons *also* have pouches with yet *even smaller* dragons inside? Is it just nesting dragons all the way down? Are we ALL inside the pouch of a giant nesting dragon at this very moment?
dragons.Goal: How does this dragon stack up to the rest of your collection?

dragons.Name: Seraph
dragons.Description:
Astounding wizards both far and near,
The 400th dragon did appear,
And in a flash of burning light,
Flew 'round the islands just a fortnight.

Best to house it while it's here,
Its billowy plumes do endear,
A visitor or wizard to take delight,
In this most regaled and splendid sight.
dragons.Goal: What a delight to be witness to the 400th dragon discovery! Surely this fiery dragon will be emblazoned onto the memories of witches and wizards everywhere!

dragons.Name: Bounteous
dragons.Description: When the harvest yields the most, bounteous dragons are always near. Witches and wizards constantly try to conjure new spells to deter these unabashed crop connoisseurs. Little do they know, these dragons are not selfish. These caring creatures are in fact making sure the hatchlings have more than enough to eat. Some bounteous dragons keep bringing treats after the babies grow into juveniles... sometimes even into adulthood.
dragons.Goal: This dragon's bounteousness knows no bounds!

dragons.Name: Teozinte
dragons.Description: Every so often the teozinte dragon sheds its scales, which are then gathered and strung into necklaces, or sewn onto wizard robes.  It's all the rage to have discarded teozinte scales on your robes during the Om of Noms, although some say the outfits do look pretty corny.
dragons.Goal: Aw shucks, there's no doubt this is quite an a-maize-ing dragon, don't you think?

dragons.Name: Bogberry
dragons.Description: While traversing the dark Flame Swamp, adventurer Weston became stuck waist-deep in the thick mud. After several hours, a weary Weston saw a dragon of unusual size begin to take shape in the mists. A bogberry dragon eventually materialized, snagged Weston by the robes, and safely pulled him out of the muck. Most magicfolk still don't believe Weston's tale of being saved by a bogberry dragon while bogged down in a bog.
dragons.Goal:
Inconceivable! You've gotten the bogberry dragon!
Maybe I'm not using that word right?

dragons.Name: Nimbus
dragons.Description: The wizard Pi Roh had a vision of the Nimbus dragon floating on clouds of miasma. Not sure what to make of this, he thought it was simply too amazing to be real. He recorded his dream in a scroll and set it away, forgetting all about the nimbus dragon. Once the Rift stabilized, the nimbus dragon reappeared to Pi Roh, this time in person! This dragon loves to float in clouds, and for ages it has called the miasma of the Rift home. Now it can float nimbly around parks everywhere!
dragons.Goal: Who knew that the once forgotten nimbus dragon was hidden in the Rift all along?

dragons.Name: Plumpkin
dragons.Description: Plumpkin dragons usually stick together, but one baby became enchanted by the Vale's horticultural expert, Gardenia. One evening while taking a sip from a nearby stream, it watched the witch cast spell after spell, moving plants, soil, and rocks in all directions. The baby was so hypnotized by the display that it forgot it was drinking. The plumpkin baby feverishly flapped its wings to get a closer look, but instead it just rolled forward, too engorged with water.
dragons.Goal: You positively have a penchant for proliferating plumpkin dragons.

dragons.Name: Krampus
dragons.Description: If little wizards and witchlings start to get too excited for the winter festivities, parents often use the krampus dragon to keep them in line. “You better behave, or the krampus dragon will gobble up all your iceberries!” is heard fairly often this time of year. Unfortunately, this gives the sweet krampus dragon an undeserved reputation. It would never eat your iceberries! That long sticky tongue is actually used to sip up sweet nectar from blossoms in the far north.
dragons.Goal: Woah! Is that tongue supposed to look like that?

dragons.Name: Candlecrown
dragons.Description: Candlecrown dragons tend to get their exercise in the crisp coolness of night. For some Valefolk, who work ‘round the clock, this can be a startling sight. With this dragon's green hide remaining hidden in the moonlight, the adorned phantasmal flames appear to float through the Vale without an owner. The busy witches and wizards, who never stop working, usually take this as a sign that they should go home and rest.
dragons.Goal: This dragon's friendship is illuminating!

dragons.Name: Kringle
dragons.Description:
The story of one of the first encounters between dragons and wizards is believed to have involved the kringle dragon:

A long time ago, in ancient times past
Arose a fierce storm with winds that did lash.

From inside the storm there came a deep moan
That frightened all folk, from small to full grown.

The moan did continue all through the night
Even when the storm passed come early morn's light.

A brave soul did leave the warmth of his home
To see what could make that sad, lonesome groan.

It didn't take long, there up in a tree
A dragon was stuck, struggling to be free.

Fetching a tool from his wagon,
The wizard quickly released the dragon.

And the dragon was freed, so it is said,
That dragon became the wizard's best friend.

And thus is the tale, or so I've been told,
Of how kringle dragons came in from the cold.
dragons.Goal: Wow!  You must have made Sandakloz's nice list to get this dragon!

dragons.Name: Woolen
dragons.Description: Woolen dragons are friendly, specifically when they need help with an itch. Rough objects, like trees and jagged rocks, suffice but a willing witch or wizard is even better. When the snow begins to fall and you feel something nuzzling against your leg, it's probably a woolen dragon asking for a good scratch. And they are, of course, great companions if you've forgotten your mittens.
dragons.Goal: These dragons have been known to change their unusual coat patterns.

dragons.Name: Sleighbell
dragons.Description: Unique tufts of fur resemble bells with a jingle, the sleighbell dragons usually befriend wizards and love to mingle. Every eve of seasonal celebration, these selfless creatures inspire great imagination.
dragons.Goal: Ring this up as a fond memory!

dragons.Name: Starshine
dragons.Description: It used to be that the winter witch, Lumi, would win the fairy light decorating contest every year. Jealous neighbors began to get suspicious; there's no way any spell could make lights shine like that! After a bit of snooping, it was discovered that Lumi wasn't using fairy lights at all, but was enticing starshine dragons to nap amongst her trees! Lumi didn't face any repercussions, though--it's now common to find a few starshine dragons helping light up huts this time of year.
dragons.Goal: This dragon will certainly brighten your park!

dragons.Name: Jingle
dragons.Description: These jolly and helpful dragons have been known to be great at hiding in surprising locations. It wasn't until Sandakloz checked his cartload of gifts -- twice -- that the sounds of the jingle dragon gave itself away! Now wizards and witches everywhere can enjoy this jolly, helpful dragon.
dragons.Goal: Well, good to know it wasn't just a ringing in my ears that I was hearing.

dragons.Name: Party
dragons.Description: The intrepid explorer Ser Rocco was traversing the Kakapo mountains when something lively caught his eye. It was a group of party dragons excited by the sight of his airship and vying for his attention! Thinking it might be his last chance to see a new dragon discovered, Ser Rocco invited several of these dragons aboard his airship. Since then, party dragons have been renowned for their bouncy, happy attitude.
dragons.Goal: I guess it's time to get this party started!

dragons.Name: Scorn
dragons.Description: The enchantress, Jolene, was researching love dragons in the Berrywhite Mountains when she discovered a scorn dragon amidst the herd. This sweet dragon happily accepted some treats from her, but as soon as the enchantress moved to offer treats to another dragon, the scorn dragon displayed… um… a different side. Apparently this dragon insists on being the center of attention and gets a little jealous if it catches you fawning over another dragon.
dragons.Goal: Make sure to stay on this dragon's good side!

dragons.Name: Smitten
dragons.Description: Smitten dragons are unique in that they form deep bonds with the first person they see after hatching. If you happen to become the target of a smitten dragon's affections, consider yourself lucky! They are among the most lovable, loyal dragons known to wizardkind. Although you'd better get used to a dragon following you around everywhere (and we mean *everywhere*!) -- the smitten dragon won't give you a minute alone, even if you just need to use the little wizard's room.
dragons.Goal: Visitors will go head-over-heels for this dragon!

dragons.Name: Sweetheart
dragons.Description: Sweeter than sugar and zazzier than spice, the sweetheart dragon is the epitome of everything nice! These dragons always make sure their habitat-mates get dragon treats before they do, give up the best napping spots to others, and take time to play with the little ones. They are so kind hearted, in fact, that you might want to make sure you don't accidentally step on any fae-bugs while walking by their habitat. It would break their sweet little hearts!
dragons.Goal: What a sweet dragon!

dragons.Name: Spritely
dragons.Description: These spry, cuddly, and inquisitive dragons are known for their natural affinity towards creative wizards and witches. Spritely dragons were originally discovered when famous dragon artist Bob Ploss was planting a grove of Happy Trees. From a nearby grove, he saw a group of spritely dragons staring at him inquisitively. Not to be outdone in curiosity, he immediately set to painting them. From then on, spritely dragons have been a mainstay to creative wizards and witches everywhere.
dragons.Goal: Who could resist these chubby charming cherubs?

dragons.Name: Tumblethorn
dragons.Description: Eons ago, tumblethorn dragons utilized their unique adaptations to glide between the harsh Sandara desert and the Mud Flats. When the Cataclysm opened the Scar of the World, it was one of the first dragons that disappeared in that event. Thankfully, it seems that at least a few tumbled into the Rift!
dragons.Goal: You'll never be lonely when you're tumbling along with the tumbling tumblethorn dragons!

dragons.Name: Satin
dragons.Description: The satin dragon's smooth scales create the illusion that it is draped in smooth and beautiful silks. Don't be fooled though, dragons don't wear clothes--they have no use for them!
dragons.Goal: I feel luxurious just looking at this dragon! It's certainly a fashionable addition to any park.

dragons.Name: Cocoahollow
dragons.Description: This velvety brown dragon hails from the hollow dens of the Theobroma hills. Its color is thought to originate from its affinity for a local rich tuber treat growing in the vicinity of the hollows. Once the wizards learned they could be coaxed out of their dens with dragon treats instead, the cocoahollow dragons have been hopping with delight ever since.
dragons.Goal: No hollow victory, this is quite the achievement for your park!

dragons.Name: Bilby
dragons.Description: The seasons of Burcadia are very curious indeed - for they are the inverse of our seasons in the Vale! When the summer sun shines down on us, cold reigns in the lands of Burcadia and the curious bilby dragons hibernate with their families beneath the frost. Likewise, just as the air turns chilly for us, the thin layers of ice recede in Burcadia and the bilby dragons emerge - so many that a whole sea of tufted ears can be seen covering the hills!
dragons.Goal: What a great listener this dragon is, always willing to lend an ear!

dragons.Name: Cumberpatch
dragons.Description: If you don't look closely, you might miss the cumberpatch dragon entirely. The dragon likes to play a clever imitation game with nearby foliage, and is easily passed over. That's why it took sleuthing wizard Benedict Holmes to originally discover this hidden dragon!
dragons.Goal: The cumberpatch dragon sure is great at hiding, just make sure you don't miss-plant it!

dragons.Name: Rosebud
dragons.Description: The tending wizards and witches of the Cadberry Meadows always knew that the surest sign of spring was the return of the rosebud dragons. A frequent sight at the Cadberry Wells, these dragons helped spread waters from the Vernal Springs over the meadows. The wizards and witches would greet the sight of these dragons by passing along just one word: "rosebud."
dragons.Goal: This dragon is sure to be a blooming boon to your park!

dragons.Name: Hooded
dragons.Description: The hooded dragon is one of the most misunderstood dragons of the vale. Outwardly fierce in appearance, hooded dragons are actually very protective of the wizards and witches to which they become attached. They're exceptionally good at hugs, maybe a bit too much so, but that certainly doesn't stop the occasional wizard from trying! We advise admiration from a distance.
dragons.Goal: The splendidly spiraled hooded dragon is a serendipitous sight to see slithering in any stately park. Some say it's simply sssensational!

dragons.Name: Yolkwing
dragons.Description: The Burcadians of the Mountain Sun first discovered the yolkwing dragon. Adrift in the Rift, it was first found by one of Kaleni's apprentices. The yolkwing's sunny disposition found an easy home in the farms and fields of Burcadians, and is happy to make its home in many park settings. The yolkwing's whimsical appearance is sure to crack up many a visitor!
dragons.Goal: I'm not eggsagerating: this dragon is eggsactly what your park needed! I couldn't be more eggcited!

dragons.Name: Misfortune
dragons.Description:
Stub your toe? Must be a misfortune dragon.
Lost your favorite scrying crystal? Misfortune dragon.
The misfortune dragon has been blamed for a lot of wizard oopsies over the years, and quite unduly! In fact, this nocturnal dragon is so rarely seen that many wizards and witches miss out on the opportunity altogether. Naturally, this means rumors of misfortune have spread over the years.

Plus everybody knows that lightning dragons are actually responsible for everything and anything going amiss.
dragons.Goal: I've heard that if a misfortune dragon crosses your path, it means that it wants you to pet its fluffy mane!

dragons.Name: Ts'aishen
dragons.Description: Sleeping for centuries, the legendary vault dragon Ts'aishen was finally roused from his slumber by the completion of the Token of Fire, Token of Luck, and the Binding of Prosperity. Drawn to your park, Ts'aishen can collect from all dragon habitats when provided with enough Abundant Essence.

dragons.Name: Starlight
dragons.Description: Every so often, witches and wizards gather to commemorate when the first stars fell and the galaxy dragons first came to the Vale. It was on one of these gatherings that the littlest witch wished upon a star to see a dragon never seen before. To everyone's surprise, the very first starlight dragon appeared then and there! From that point onwards this dragon has been an omen of serendipity and good luck.
dragons.Goal: Amazing! A starlight dragon! You don't suppose it's actually a good luck omen, do you?

dragons.Name: Glimmerwing
dragons.Description: While performing late night crystal scrying in her observatory, the astronomancer Valentina heard a curious sound coming from outside. There she saw a wondrous sight: a glimmerwing dragon had become enthralled by one of the many crystal globes placed about the observatory. Cooing and awing at its own reflection, the dragon hardly noticed as Valentina recorded all she could before the dragon departed into the night. Since then, wizards and witches have always lit up at the chance to see these rare nighttime wonders.
dragons.Goal: A rare sight indeed to glimpse upon a glimmerwing dragon, and even rarer that it should roost in your park. Well done!

dragons.Name: Opulent
dragons.Description: It's said that opulent dragons were once the guardians of the mythical treasure city of Seebolah. Because of this, they were long thought to be a portent of prosperity and good fortune. Though Seebolah has long since been buried by time, opulent dragons still possess quite the preference for guarding piles of treasure.
dragons.Goal: I've heard wizards opine that the opulent dragon is mighty fine!

dragons.Name: Scarab
dragons.Description: This gold-scaled dragon has a special affinity for trinkets and baubles that it finds in its natural surroundings. Scarab dragons have been known to carry their trinkets with them for long distances just to feel at home. Unsurpisingly, this dragon is happiest when kept in a shiny, treasure-laden habitat.
dragons.Goal: This fabulously faceted dragon is a find worthy of the finest dragon fancier!

dragons.Name: Djinni
dragons.Description:
After spending one thousand and one nights searching the Sandarra Desert for treasure, the traveler Ala Din came across the fabled Cave of Wanderers. Though the cave was filled with fascinating and jeweled treasure, he became transfixed on a somewhat grimy lamp. Overtaken by the need to shine it up a bit, he suddenly found himself in front of a djinni dragon.

Having heard rumors of such fantastical creatures from legend, he did the first thing that came to mind: he wished for more wishes. This was of course against the rules of magic, and immediately and forever stripped the djinni dragons of any wish-granting powers they might have had.
dragons.Goal: This dragon is so spectacular that you might find yourself wishing for another. But that might take some time...

dragons.Name: Regal
dragons.Description: Originally from the Palagos islands, these dragons had to stand out amidst the vibrant tropical colors in order to even be seen by their own kind. Thanks to that extravagant plumage, it's hard to miss the regal dragon! Even if you do, the majestic behavior of this dragon is sure to make itself noticed in front of any wizard or witch.
dragons.Goal: Magnificent! Your park has never looked fancier than with a regal dragon!

dragons.Name: Fireflight
dragons.Description: Mornings are majestic for magicfolk who awake at dawn. Even at night their wings don't rest. Their involuntary behavior forms a makeshift tent to protect the creatures from rain and snow, but the prolonged formation lifts them into the air by sunrise. They serenely float along until gentle breezes rouse the dragons and they descend to start their day. Early risers in the Vale boast the beauty of this daily ritual but jealous friends say they're full of hot air.
dragons.Goal: Light as the breeze and always aims to please, the fireflight dragon isn't just hot air!

dragons.Name: Snowflake 6
dragons.Description: They say every snowflake is unique, and some snowflakes are more unique than others! Just when Lumi thought she had discovered the rarest of the snowflake dragons, along came another snowflake dragon! "As you can see, this dragon is nothing like the other snowflake dragons," she said. The wizards and witches were so impressed that they dubbed this dragon "snowflake dragon" to honor the occasion.
dragons.Goal: Fantabulous! I've never seen a finer flake!

dragons.Name: Dartwing
dragons.Description: Baby dartwing dragons almost never settle down. They zip around checking brightly colored hats for sweet nectar but will sometimes knock one to the ground amid their zealous efforts. Wizards with dirty hats consistently mistake this for a mischevious spell and young Valers usually catch the blame. A slight hum that accompanies the ruckus is the only clue to the identity of the true culprit.
dragons.Goal: I'm sure the other wizards and witches will be simply abuzz about this dragon!

dragons.Name: Sandscale
dragons.Description: If you're taking a stroll on a beach, keep watch for sandscale dragons soaking up the sun. If you accidentally step on an outstretched wing, these dragons will let you know you've crossed a line. Their reaction is no more than a startling grunt but it has rubbed a few wizards the wrong way. Even though sandscale dragons don't hold grudges, some Valefolk still claim they are a little rough around the edges.
dragons.Goal: They say that sand is coarse, rough, irritating, and gets everywhere... but I simply love this sandscale dragon!

dragons.Name: Tidepool
dragons.Description:
The idea of an ocean is lost on many Valers living in the sky, but there is a group that analyzed this murky myth. Their fascination led to experiments which led to more questions: “Would it be dangerous to attempt a manifestation of such a large body of water?” They reduced the power of the incantation and safely conjured a small pool of ocean water. The spell needed hours to finish so the group came back after a long meal.

When they returned, they were delighted to see bright vegetation and moving marine life. As soon as a witch dipped her hand in to confirm the stability of the spell, everything moved and a face popped out. It was a dragon! The magicfolk didn't know if they had attracted the unknown creature or created it from thin air. They archived that mystery for later reflection and spread the news of the miraculous tidepool dragon.
dragons.Goal: Notice how remarkably clean the shells and starfish are on this dragon. That's a surefire sign you've got a tidepool dragon.

dragons.Name: Abraxas
dragons.Description: Abraxas dragons love treats as much as the next dragon, but sometimes they want an extra jolt. When dark clouds roll in, abraxas dragons gather side-by-side in open fields. When they're lucky, lightning strikes one dragon and electricity surges through the rest. Every dragon gets in on the surge of energy. Sometimes this tactic doesn't work, but only if a firefly dragon gets stuck in the grid. It bugs them a bit, but it's not too shocking.
dragons.Goal: I'm shocked! I never thought I'd see one of these archons of lightning in person. Surely this is a discovery that will electrify your visitors!

dragons.Name: Sunscorch
dragons.Description: Sunscorch dragons live up to their name. They seek out warmth and bask in it until their thermochromic scales transform. Shade can help revert them back and water is just as effective. If you prefer your Ami'Lya Pond to be full of water, maybe move it away from a sunscorch dragon looking to cool off; their tails can make rather large splashes.
dragons.Goal: Amazing! The sunscorch dragon alters its scales depending on whether it's exposed to day or night. This should be quite the sight for visitors of any hour!

dragons.Name: Chromacorn
dragons.Description: Once upon a time, in the far away kingdom of Whitedragon, there lived a fair princess named Eris who was said to have the purest of hearts. One day, Eris was in the woods collecting wildflowers when she came upon a peaceful clearing with a still crystal pond. A chromacorn dragon, previously thought to be legend, stood gazing at its reflection in the waters; it appeared to be stuck in a trance, mesmerized by its own beauty! Eris spoke patiently to the dragon, being careful not to startle the creature, and eventually freed the chromacorn dragon from its trance.  To thank the fair maiden, the dragon flew her back to the Whitedragon castle to astonished onlookers, and there they lived happily ever after as best friends.
dragons.Goal: This dragon's color is so nice and bright that you might think all the world's a sunny day!

dragons.Name: Eve
dragons.Description:
The eve dragon has an almost ethereal air to it, showing off an impressive set of wing colors that resemble winter sunrises o'er the crystalline valleys of Silverfalls Gorge. In fact, ancient legend suggests it was the eve dragon that broke the long dark of the first winter.

So it goes, after weeks of winter darkness, a beam of light descended from the sky to illuminate the highest peak of the mountains surrounding Silverfalls Gorge. There in the beam was an eve dragon, who spread its magnificent wings in welcome of the sleepy sun as it peeked above the horizon.

Today, Valefolk attribute such stories to old witches' tales, but nevertheless find themselves in a state of quiet awe when in the presence of this alluring dragon.
dragons.Goal: I forecast that this dragon will bring your visitors a lot of mirth!

dragons.Name: Sprite
dragons.Description: This dragon has a peculiar head. It has been said, from this head, pours the most ridiculous banter. The problem is, a meticulous canter can be the downfall of an inane jester, whose primary joy will only fester. Tricks are its mainstay, jokes are plain play. Sprite dragon's head is floating, but don't fret. It won't stray.
dragons.Goal: This dragon possesses amazing magical properties! Just don't lose your head over how amazing they are.

dragons.Name: Kaiju
dragons.Description: The kaiju dragon is the strongest known dragon in all the vale. Witnesses swear they've seen a pack of kaiju dragons pulling entire mountain ranges in their wake, just as casually as you might pull a cart of robes. The larger mystery is what the kaiju dragons intend to do with an entire mountain range.
dragons.Goal: We're ninety percent certain that kaiju dragons aren't going to trample their habitats. Better keep a close eye on your dragon, just in case. For science... magic science.

dragons.Name: Oracle
dragons.Description: The oracle dragon is so named for its blind stare, as if gazing into another realm. Long ago, wizards and witches revered the oracle dragon, bringing it food and pettings in exchange for good fortune. Whether the oracle dragon really can see into the future is beyond current understanding, but it doesn't hurt to befriend this dragon, just in case.
dragons.Goal: I don't think anybody saw this dragon coming!

dragons.Name: Totem
dragons.Description: Rumors abound when it comes to the epic totem dragons. Some people believe the totem dragon was first carved from wood, then brought to life by the world's most powerful ancient wizards. Others believe the totem dragon is no dragon at all, but in fact a spirit in disguise, biding its time until it can reveal its true form. As far as the wizards and witches can tell, the totem dragon is surely awesome-looking, but probably just a regular epic dragon. Probably.
dragons.Goal: This dragon is certainly a chip off the old block!

dragons.Name: Osteryx
dragons.Description: Dragons of a feather, flock together… unless they're osteryx dragons. These silly, soaring scavengers are crazy about stunts. With all their quirks and quickness, it would actually be dangerous if they attempted to fly in formation. If you observe this zany display, be sure to applaud: silent gawkers really ruffle their scales.
dragons.Goal: Looks like this one is going to make dragon afficionados have to bone up on their dragon knowledge!

dragons.Name: Bonescale
dragons.Description: Little was known about the icy Caves of Ramora in the northern wastelands until an adventurous group of dragonologists set out to search for clues of ancient dragon life. While excavating the caves, a young wizard named Garant became excited when he unearthed a fully intact dragon skull! You can imagine his surprise when the skull began to move, followed by a long neck, wings, tail, oh my! It was a living dragon! Other bonescale dragons began to dig themselves out of the earth, curious to greet the newcomers and more than happy to accept a few treats. It turns out that bonescale dragons love to burrow into the earth to keep warm in the icy north. Clever dragons.
dragons.Goal: Don't get the cold shoulder from this hardheaded dragon!

dragons.Name: Hakahaka
dragons.Description: Legend tells of the Warrior Witch Malina and her beloved hakahaka dragon. The two were always seen together until the events of The Cataclysm separated them. Determined to find her missing friend, Malina scoured The Surface - the wild magics of The Cataclysm swirling about her - traversing landscapes filled with volcanic eruptions, sailing across deadly seas, and battling never-before-seen magical enchantments. After several weeks Malina nearly gave into despair while fending off an army of enchanted coconuts when her hakahaka dragon, like a rock crashing down a mountain, appeared by her side and plowed through the coconuts. To this day it is said that the swirling pattern of the hakahaka dragon's hide is a result of the swirling wild magics that it encountered during The Cataclysm. To this day it's also known that hakahaka dragons love coconuts.
dragons.Goal: You're welcome.

dragons.Name: Embossed
dragons.Description: With the stars shining bright overhead, the young musician, Rella, decided to take some time on the anniversary of the Vale to ponder and celebrate the last seven years. She found a calm meadow and began to play her harp and became lost in the music. She played for several hours until she heard a harmony join her chorus. The young witch looked for the source of the sweet music and was awed to see an embossed dragon had joined her, using the strings strung on its tail to accompany the music. The song continued into the night -- witch and dragon celebrating not only past years, but bright ones to come.
dragons.Goal: A dragon is the best Birthday present!

dragons.Name: Honuhonu
dragons.Description: Valefolk were surprised when the young wizard, Warren, came home from swimming one day with a never-before-seen dragon in tow. Curious as to how Warren befriended this Honuhonu Dragon, an interview was set up with the young wizard to hear his story. The poor kid had such a bad case of stage fright, the only thing he could say throughout the entire 1-hour interview was “I like Honuhonus.”
dragons.Goal: Dude! This dragon is totally awesome!

dragons.Name: Humuhumu
dragons.Description: Humuhumu dragons are known for their remarkable ability to forget things. It's rather endearing to watch a Humuhumu dragon meet a little witchling, only to forget a few minutes later, then get excited to meet the same witchling over and over again. Of course, this does mean that you need to watch how often Humuhumu dragons eat – they forget that they've eaten and just keep eating!
dragons.Goal: This dragon is sure to make a splash!

dragons.Name: Limulimu
dragons.Description: Nobody really believed it when the self-proclaimed dragon expert, Dustin McBurr, came back from the Crimson Sea announcing he had discovered a new dragon. It was just like that time he had insisted he had seen an invisible dragon--preposterous! It wasn't until McBurr appeared in the middle of town, still covered in the Crimson Sea's briny water, with a happy little limulimu dragon by his side that valers had to acknowledge his discovery.
dragons.Goal: No one can say you're wet behind the ears with this dragon in your park!

dragons.Name: Manomano
dragons.Description: The wizard Marty Sheill was fishing along the Armity Coast when he hooked the largest fish that ever existed. It took 12 hours to reel in the creature (although this number gets larger with each telling), when out of the roiling waters leaped an impossible sight -- a manomano dragon, not a fish, had been hooked! According to Marty the dragon was so huge it blotted out the sun, causing the very stars to be seen in its shadow. It seems the 12 hours was nothing but play for the dragon as it simply snapped the line and leapt back into the waves. Of course, not everyone believes Marty's tale; some say it's just a bunch of hoo ha.
dragons.Goal: You're gonna need a bigger park!

dragons.Name: Corrupticorn
dragons.Description:
During a midnight stroll searching for firefly dragons, princess Eris thought she left her chromacorn dragon friend at home. She didn't realize her clingy companion followed her into the woods until she caught sight of it rummaging in a blushroom patch. When the chromacorn dragon couldn't find any bright blue snacks, it reared up and roared. Under the full moon, a dark purple shimmer spread over the dragon and transformed it into something new… the corrupticorn dragon! Eris said aloud, “I never knew dragons could get hangry”.

*Collect and place 10 unique Flames to perform the ritual with a chromacorn dragon
dragons.Goal: Everyone has a dark side...

dragons.Name: Chimneypuff
dragons.Description: There's only one type of dragon that is drawn to the smell of a failed fire spell. When Valers can't complete a combustible conjuration, chimneypuff dragons congregate. Three or four… or even five of them will swoop down into your chimney and plop out into the fireplace. Here, they'll gather and cough tiny fireballs to help ignite the kindling. Once the blaze is burning bright, they bow their heads, shake off a bit of soot, and flutter to the next cottage. Some folk even reward these hearth-helpers with a spoonful of sugar.
dragons.Goal: Warming hearts and homes throughout the Vale.

dragons.Name: Porcelain
dragons.Description:
Bone dragons are a mainstay of the Vale and have been revered for years, but one wizard loved them so much that he developed a spell to manifest this idolization. The wizard was named Feldspar and his cosmetic conjuration was a success! A plated sheen with ornate designs coated a willing bone dragon volunteer and transfigured it into a porcelain dragon. Both wizard and dragon were delighted with the outcome. When asked about altering a dragon in such a cavalier and mischievous fashion, Feldspar's eyes glazed over with boredom.

*Collect and place 10 unique Ornaments to perform the ritual with a bone dragon
dragons.Goal: Some skeletons prefer makeovers.

dragons.Name: Wrath
dragons.Description:
Love dragons enjoy company, but they have to travel all the way from Berrywhite Mountain and down to the Vale to satiate that strong need. Unfortunately, some dragons get lost on the journey. This happened to one particular love dragon and its burden of solitude had a dramatic effect. Its hide turned gray and its scales hardened, devolving into the newly discovered wrath dragon. It eventually made it to the Vale and was ecstatic to be amongst magicfolk, but the witches and wizards recoiled as it galloped in with a giant grin. As they do, a group of love dragons came to console their pal and surrounded it with pure compassion. This helped changed the Valers' perception of this uniquely unnerving creature.

*Collect and place 10 unique Tendrils to perform the ritual with a love dragon
dragons.Goal: What is never loved, is lost.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Fire
dragons.Description:
This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond.
When you think of dragons, the fierce fire dragon is probably at the forefront of your thoughts. It is true that these beasts get cranky when they get cold. All you have to do is keep them in a warm place and they become as harmless as the ground beneath their feet! Never mind that their feet are typically found above active volcanoes.
Opposite: Cold
dragons.Goal: Truly an icon of the dragon world!

dragons.Name: Chitin
dragons.Description: A parched baby chitin dragon once wandered through the wilderness searching for a puddle of water. It heard a drip, drip, drip, licked its lips, and spun around. The purple dragon saw nothing except for low hanging tree branches and vines. DRIP! The dragon heard it again, but this time it saw a shimmer of water beyond the vines. There was a small cave housing a fresh rain puddle, still dripping from a storm. The baby chitin dragon sprinted toward the vines, hoping to break through and enjoy a cool drink. Instead, it tripped, rolled into a ball, and sailed right through the cave and out the other side. It landed in a mud puddle and was covered in muck. It shrugged and took a huge sludgy slurp.
dragons.Goal: The hardest exterior houses the softest heart.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Earth
dragons.Description:
This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Despite the harshness of their habitat, the earth dragon is the least restless of all known breeds. They are supremely well adapted for their desert homes with thick skin and large bodies to store water. The spikes on their back offer protection from predators, but honestly, what animal in its right mind would think to take on one of these massive beasts?
Opposite: Air
dragons.Goal: Imposing spikes belie a down-to-earth nature.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Lava
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. The lava dragon was the first to undeniably establish that some dragons use magic to fly. While its wings are more than enough to bring it aloft as a juvenile, they remain the same size throughout its life. This creates a somewhat awkward looking adult appearance that it probably wouldn't enjoy you pointing out.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Obsidian
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Found in the volcanic regions of Wrothmoore, the obsidian dragon's iridescent horns are sure to make it one of your visitors' favorite new dragons!

dragons.Name: Ghostly Cold
dragons.Description:
This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. The cold dragon is revered in the northern countries where people will often worship them and offer them food in exchange for protection. Some tribes refer to them as the grandfathers of the north because of the signature fur that grows near the front of their mouths. This is the most intelligent of all the common dragon breeds known.
Opposite: Fire
dragons.Goal: Their impressive beards have earned them the nickname 'great-grandfathers of the North'.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Glacier
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Tremendous eaters, glacier dragons follow the first rule of geography, never get separated from your lunch. Trails of excess water in your habitat?  We assure you that's meltwater, not an accident.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Mountain
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. The mountain dragon is a solitary beast, found wandering the frozen highlands to the north. Its long horns and shielded back protect it from, well, everything. Since nothing threatens it, it is one of the calmest dragons around.

dragons.Name: Auroch
dragons.Description: The few magicfolk who have seen an auroch dragon, know full well to steer clear. These hefty creatures love to spend their unbridled energy running circles in dense fields of grass and wildflowers. With as many horns as it has, no witch or wizard would risk catching a glimpse of this ritual. When a meadow is mowed down to a single pile of vegetation, what's left for an auroch dragon to do? Jump in the mess, of course! This could be the only time these dragons smile, but no one is willing to walk into the bullseye of a mysterious crop circle to find out.
dragons.Goal: Don't judge a dragon by its horns.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Bone
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Bone dragons can only be found for a couple weeks during the year. The rest of the year it is believed that they burrow underground near cemeteries to be around other bones. But I bet if you breed one and put it in a habitat with other bones, it would stick around. Or perhaps near a heat source to keep away the bone-chilling winter cold?

dragons.Name: Ghostly Ghost
dragons.Description:
It was once believed to be a prank played on young Valers... but a ghostly ghost dragon is no joke.

There was a group of young magicfolk who loved mysteries, yet they never solved one. Most of the time, they would gather just to eat loads of treats. Of course, when they least expected it, they saw a ghostly ghost dragon emerge from a foggy forest. Candy fell out of their mouths and they ran. They didn't realize the dragon only wanted to share some more spooky snacks.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Spectre
dragons.Description:
This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond.

Once upon a dark night foggy, Nogard awoke, worn and groggy,
And looked about at scrolls and tomes of ancient dragon lore.
While he drifted, nearly sleeping, came a sound, the sound of creaking,
A sound as if some thing were sneaking, sneaking near his tower door.
“‘Tis some visitor”, he mumbled, “creeping in the foggy moor-
Only this, and nothing more.”

Gath'ring his courage (and his beard) Nogard stood to see what neared,
And looked out his tower window at the distant foggy moor.
Then a form came from the dark, ghostly pallored, eerily stark,
A shade which made Nogard remark, “What dread awaits me, in my park?”
He grabbed his cloak and staff and said, “There's only one way to be sure.”
And then he walked upon the moor.

From the dark there came a grumble, a soft and low kind of rumble,
Nogard almost took a stumble, out in the foggy moor.
Nogard peered into the black, and what he saw took him aback,
A hungry spectre dragon pack, to which he sighed and threw a snack.
Nogard called out to the dragons as he walked back to the door,
“That's all you get, and nothing more!”

dragons.Name: Ghostly Spirit
dragons.Description: Some might say spirit dragons are the pinnacle of paranormal perception. Other Valefolk don't realize the truth is still out there. Ghostly spirit dragons do exist, but you must want to see them to experience ethereal enlightenment.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Decay
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. The decay dragon is the star of a spooky bedtime story in the Vale, giving it somewhat of an unfair reputation. Parents tell their children not to play tricks, or else the decay dragon will drag them from their beds and bring them to a horrible land without candy! In reality, though, the decay dragon's interests are more about eating treats, and less about dragging little witches and wizards off into the night.

dragons.Name: Ghostly Nosferatu
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Originally discovered by the powerful wizard Whitbee, the nosferatu dragon possesses an impressive pair of sweet teeth! However, there is no need to be frightened, as their propensity to bite can be satisfied by dragon treats!

dragons.Name: Ghostly Oni
dragons.Description: This ancestral dragon was summoned from realms beyond. Oni dragons may look like they can live in any stark environment, but in actuality they love a comfortable den made of found objects around the Vale. Leaves, scraps of yarn, and even discarded Valefolk clothing are ideal for their makeshift bedding. Gwyddion the Great Nogard claims to have seen one lash out during this odd ritual. The oni dragon was diligently crafting its sleeping quarters when tree branches whirled in from a westward wind and decimated the dragon's hard work. The oni dragon drew its club-like tail back and, with one fell swoop, shattered them into a thousand pieces. It is rumored that the oni dragon smirked and started over again.

dragons.Name: Vidalia
dragons.Description: There is a dragon that can make you think twice, with nothing more than a look. It may appear this creature has no care to give, but here's a secret, it does. Vidalia dragons, prim and proper, will help you clean up and put your best foot forward. If you're not expecting it, their surprising generosity might even make you cry.
dragons.Goal: Layer on the compliments when caring for this creature

dragons.Name: Curlyleaf
dragons.Description: Baby curlyleaf dragons are some of the cutest in the Vale, but they avoid magicfolk regularly. An adult dragon can duck behind its broad wings if it cares not to engage in social activities, but a baby is just a tuft of green with nowhere to hide. If a verdant ball is seen rolling down a hill, it's safe to assume it's a shy curlyleaf baby escaping an awkward situation.
dragons.Goal: Get ahead with good nature

dragons.Name: Karroot
dragons.Description: If you've ever gardened or tended to a farm, you're probably aware of the vigilant karroot dragon. They tend to travel in large groups and offer farmers a service to guard their crops. Their keen eyesight hones in on any suspicious behavior. This creates quite the scene when a sneaky Vale youth tries to steal a fresh snack. Never has anyone seen such a flurry of orange and green, unless they're still feeling the effects of Whitbee's Candy Bash.
dragons.Goal: What a sight for sore eyes!

dragons.Name: Bloatato
dragons.Description: Bloatato dragons can be somewhat oblivious, but don't assume they just sit around. There was once a sweating, hot bloatato dragon that was approximately four hops away from a shimmering puddle. It sat there staring at it for maybe an hour, yet it never made one wiggle toward the water. Then, with one swift action, it spread its scrawny wings and feverishly flapped. It made the short journey, stopped flying, and plummeted down into the puddle. Some say the dragon was so hot it sizzled as soon as it dropped.
dragons.Goal: Are your eyes bigger than your stomach?

dragons.Name: Aubergine
dragons.Description: Even though aubergine dragons share an ancestral connection with nightshade dragons, they couldn't be more different. Our purple pals have a propensity to plunge prematurely into eruptions of giggles. It's a rare occasion that anyone understands the inspiration for such guffaws. Instead, bystanders try to egg it on for even bigger belly laughs.
dragons.Goal: The dragon formerly known as eggplant

dragons.Name: Libretto
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 4

Meanwhile in the Vale, a crooning chorus walked down a snowy path, giving houses and the families inside a sample of their jolly carols. Their angelic voices rang throughout the town and intrigued a nearby libretto dragon. It peeked and saw the travelling singers, but didn't want to be left out. The curious creature followed the tunes, but stayed a few steps behind to remain unseen. When the group hit a high note, the libretto dragon couldn't restrain its enthusiasm and let out a squawk for the ages. The troop of troubadours spun around hastily to see a bashful dragon wanting to be included. They welcomed it with kind gestures and invited it to join as they kept on spreading cheer…
dragons.Goal: Now that you found this dragon, sing it loud and proud!

dragons.Name: Nibwhip
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 1

On a cold and blustery night, several Valers gathered to concoct a hot drink to warm the soul. It was chocolaty and creamy and required constant stirring to keep the perfect consistency. A nibwhip dragon waddled out from behind a rock, sniffing and gulping the air. The witches and wizards welcomed it and promised a taste if it helped stir the delicate brew. The nibwhip dragon obliged and stirred through the night while the magicfolk went home to rest up for the festivities in the morrow. Little did the dragon know; there was something lurking in a nearby forest. The sounds of branches breaking and leaves scattering circled the cauldron and the tasty drink…
dragons.Goal: Some say, you are what you eat, but does that apply to drinks?

dragons.Name: Sugarplum
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 6

That very same night, a sugarplum dragon wandered in search of flowers that reflected the moonlight. It came across a cluster of lunar-luminescent lilies that inspired the dragon to grin and skip. It plucked some and placed them between scales and fur to enhance its luster. It let out a happy little chirp. A barrage of footsteps grew louder and louder until an avarice dragon appeared at the peak of anger. The sugarplum dragon recoiled, but soon saw the red, droopy eyes and sullen stance of the creature. The sugarplum dragon approached the weary one and saw its unforgiving living quarters. In no time at all, the sugarplum dragon had gathered straw and grass to form a much more comfortable bed for the avarice dragon. The avarice dragon inspected the bed as if it were a trap, then placed one paw gently on the bedding. It was soft. The avarice dragon plopped down and sighed heavily. The sugarplum dragon was so delighted it leaped and twirled with glee. Incidentally, this celebratory dance hypnotized the avarice dragon into a deep sleep.
dragons.Goal: A perfect pirouette would almost require wings...

dragons.Name: Avarice
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 5

In a deep dark cave, an avarice dragon lay tossing and turning on a bed of DragonCash. It appeared that slumbering comfort was greatly out of reach for this poor bedraggled being. Finally, it had found the perfect spot and its eyelids slowly closed. As soon as a genuine snore bellowed out of its snout, the loudest squawk in the Vale echoed everywhere. The avarice dragon's eyes popped open; it stood straight up, and banged its head on a low-hanging stalactite. It groaned and snarled with hackles standing on end. It marched toward the mouth of the cave to find the cause of its unpleasant awakening, yet there was nothing there. It took flight and soared over the Vale until it spotted a boisterous choir and a contributing libretto dragon. It let out a giant roar that scattered the singers and even made the libretto dragon hide. Satisfied, the avarice dragon flew back home to its cave…
dragons.Goal: You can't get no... satisfaction-- oh wait, you got it!

dragons.Name: Burglehoo
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 8

When wizards speak about burglehoo dragons, it always has a sharp tone. No one knows what to expect with these creatures, but they have been seen slinking and stalking with the intention of remaining hidden. There is a family that will attest that these dragons have hearts that grow three times bigger than any magicfolk. This family was hungry and their fireplace had grown cold. They couldn't get a flame lit with magic nor muscle. A burglehoo dragon just happened to pass and saw that these folks needed more than a little help. BOOM! Just then, a gumdrop flare fanned in the sky and this dragon knew just what to do. It snuck its way through the Vale until it saw an entire table filled with goodies. While a sugary plume clouded the confections, the burglehoo dragon slithered on its belly and snuck under the table undetected.

Only a few moments later, the hungry family heard a knock on their door. When they opened it, they saw a sweet feast waiting for them on a large table. They also saw the table had been dragged in the snow for some distance, accompanied by dragon tracks.
dragons.Goal: You've found the strength of ten burglehoos, plus two!

dragons.Name: Gulletail
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 2

Sometimes, even dragons can get lost in a forest. If their wings are too stiff to fly above the treetops, it can cause quite the panic... it's even worse if they have no wings at all. This happened to one unfortunate gulletail dragon, as it wandered and shivered in the night, looking for any relief from the bitter cold. It smelled what could only be a hot treat and followed its nose to a clearing. It found an oblivious nibwhip dragon stirring a witch's cauldron, billowing with steam. The gulletail dragon circled the clearing, trying to distract the helpful dragon with ominous noises. The nibwhip dragon finally broke its concentration and left the cauldron unattended to search for the cause of the ruckus. The gulletail dragon licked its lips and slithered toward the chocolaty goodness…
dragons.Goal: Farm to table then tail to mouth...

dragons.Name: Saccharine
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 7

If there's one dragon that will help magicfolk make delectable edibles, it's the saccharine dragon. Some say its breath has amazing powers to sweeten anything on a plate. Others say it only needs to be in the vicinity of food for flavors to be enhanced. But on this magical night, the famous Confection Coven needed all the help they could get. They sent up a gumdrop flare to signal any nearby saccharine dragons and luckily one came to the rescue. When it arrived, it took one look at a table filled with burned cookies, melted candies, and drooping cakes. It exhaled a single blast of magic that exploded in a shower of sprinkles and icing. When the sugar cleared, the table was bursting with perfect desserts that now almost looked too good to eat. The coven gazed at the miracle, but was suddenly startled by a loud thud under the table. It bumped again and they all scattered in fear the saccharine dragon's power was about to backfire…
dragons.Goal: Success is so sweet when paired with this dragon.

dragons.Name: Lokilure
dragons.Description:
Winter Saga: Chapter 3

High in the treetops is where lokilure dragons love to perch. They tend to prefer a view of everyone and everything. No one knows the reason why, but one example has helped to clarify this question. On the eve of the first great celebration, a lokilure dragon spotted a gulletail dragon inches away from gulping down an entire batch of chocolate brew. It had seen magicfolk and even a nibwhip dragon working on it all night, so it decided to trick the thieving creature and preserve the dedication invested in the work. It shook its horns and tail to mimic a dinner bell Valers often used. The gulletail dragon perked up with stomach grumbling, and sped off toward the sound of the bell. The lokilure dragon snickered as it watched from above.
